title.en: The Substance of Concern (SOC) module of the EU DPP core ontology proposed by the CIRPASS-2 European project.

description.en:
MODULE: SOC
Substances of Concern module of the  EU DPP core ontology proposal of the CIRPASS-2 European project.

DEPENDENCIES:  This module has dependencies to the following EU DPP Core Ontology (CO) modules: CON, P_DPP.  

The third iteration of the Substances of Concern module of the EU DPP core ontology proposal of the CIRPASS-2 European project.

The information requirements laid out in ESPR Art 7(2) and Art 7(5) for products require the information requirements to make it possible to track the substances of concern, throughout the life cycle of the products concerned. These information requirements for specific product groups are specified in the delegated acts adopted pursuant to Art 4 of ESPR.
	
This module addresses only the information requirements referred and stated in the ESPR. 
=====================================
CONTEXT: 
Regulation (EC) No 1907/2006  Art 3(1) defines Substance: means a chemical element and its compounds in the natural state or obtained by
any manufacturing process, including any additive necessary to preserve its stability and any impurity deriving from the process used, but excluding any solvent which may be separated without affecting the stability of the substance or changing its composition;

sourceStatus.value: ESPR-grounded ontology modelling abstraction; this RDF resource is not itself a term defined by the Regulation.

comment.en: An instruction concerning the management of a substance of concern in its SubstancePresence context, including safe use, disassembly, preparation for reuse, reuse, recycling and environmentally sound end-of-life management. This domain-specific modelling abstraction supports the information elements in ESPR Article 7(5)(d)-(e); it is not a term defined by the Regulation and does not determine legal obligations or applicability.

sourceStatus.value: Controlled vocabulary representing the four legal qualification branches of ESPR Article 2(27).

comment.en: Legal qualification criteria corresponding to points (a)-(d) of ESPR Article 2(27). A substance may satisfy more than one criterion.

sourceStatus.value: representation of an information element explicitly required by the cited ESPR provision; the RDF resource itself is an ontology modelling construct.

comment.en: A concentration reported as an interval with a minimum and a maximum numerical value. The measurement unit is provided through dpp:hasMeasurementUnit.

sourceStatus.value: direct legal definition reproduced from the cited legislation.

comment.en: A chemical substance used as the generic superclass for substance identity and naming information. In this SOC module it primarily supports the modelling of dpp:SubstanceOfConcern; its presence does not make SOC a general-purpose substance-reporting module.

sourceStatus.value: ESPR-grounded ontology modelling abstraction; this RDF resource is not itself a term defined by the Regulation.

comment.en: A contextual relation entity representing the presence of a substance in relation to a product as placed on the market, including a product, component or spare part. It enables product-dependent location, concentration and instruction information to be represented without treating those data as intrinsic characteristics of the substance itself or classifying the presence as a product property. In the CORE profile the modelling pattern is one SubstancePresence per reported location when different locations require different concentrations; sector-specific extensions may provide explicit reference bases for several calculation perspectives. This class is an ontology modelling abstraction supporting ESPR Article 7(5), rather than a term explicitly defined by the Regulation.

sourceStatus.value: Implementation measurement-unit convention; not a named SI Digital Framework unit PID.

references.value: SI style convention: percent denotes the number 0.01; mass fraction values should be represented as decimal ratios in data.

comment.en: Project-managed measurement-unit convention for dimensionless mass fraction expressed as a decimal ratio of masses. Use dpp:numericalValue "0.001"^^xsd:decimal for 0.1 % by mass. This avoids encoding "w/w" in the unit symbol and may be replaced by an official SI Digital Framework PID if one becomes available.

sourceStatus.value: direct legal definition reproduced from the cited legislation.

comment.en: A substance that: (a) meets the criteria laid down in Article 57 of Regulation (EC) No 1907/2006 and is identified in accordance with Article 59(1) of that Regulation; (b) is classified in Part 3 of Annex VI to Regulation (EC) No 1272/2008 in one of the following hazard classes or hazard categories: (i) carcinogenicity categories 1 and 2; (ii) germ cell mutagenicity categories 1 and 2; (iii) reproductive toxicity categories 1 and 2; (iv) endocrine disruption for human health categories 1 and 2; (v) endocrine disruption for the environment categories 1 and 2; (vi) persistent, mobile and toxic or very persistent, very mobile properties; (vii) persistent, bioaccumulative and toxic or very persistent, very bioaccumulative properties; (viii) respiratory sensitisation category 1; (ix) skin sensitisation category 1; (x) hazardous to the aquatic environment — categories chronic 1 to 4; (xi) hazardous to the ozone layer; (xii) specific target organ toxicity — repeated exposure categories 1 and 2; (xiii) specific target organ toxicity — single exposure categories 1 and 2; (c) is regulated under Regulation (EU) 2019/1021; or (d) negatively affects the reuse and recycling of materials in the product in which it is present.

sourceStatus.value: ESPR-grounded modelling construct for recording an explicit Article 2(27) qualification; the assertion is not itself a legal term and the ontology does not infer legal status.

comment.en: A documented, explicit assertion that a substance satisfies one or more non-exclusive qualification criteria in ESPR Article 2(27). For criterion (d), the applicable product context is represented by a dpp:SubstancePresence linked through dpp:hasApplicableQualification. This modelling construct records asserted qualification evidence; it does not infer legal status.
